research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: direct official GOV.UK Forestry Commission/MHCLG Planning Data verification, current 2026 dates where present, TPO/hedgerow/felling/EIA/grant/consultation/provenance separation, indicative-vs-exact geometry, funding-vs-consent and forestry-vs-planning fail-closed gates. Not parcel-level accuracy.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification plus repository duplicate searches

official_sources.name: Tree Preservation Orders and trees in conservation areas
official_sources.fact: MHCLG planning guidance explains making, confirming, varying and revoking TPOs and applications/appeals for works to protected trees.
official_sources.gate: A TPO guidance page or map signal is not proof of the exact live order, protected tree geometry, consent or permitted works for a parcel.

official_sources.name: Countryside hedgerow protection: removing hedgerows
official_sources.fact: Natural England/Defra guidance requires the applicable countryside hedgerow removal process and describes LPA retention/removal notices and the 42-day response period.
official_sources.gate: Hedgerow presence, notice submission or silence assumptions must not be promoted to lawful removal without exact applicability, dates and notice status.

official_sources.name: Tree felling: getting permission
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission guidance updated 21 August 2025 explains felling licences, exemptions, other controls, restocking and penalties.
official_sources.gate: A felling licence or an exemption does not remove other planning, TPO, conservation-area, wildlife or environmental permissions.

official_sources.name: Apply for a felling licence
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission guidance published 8 July 2026 sets the current application route, licence periods, post-licence duties and appeal route.
official_sources.gate: An application, service status or processing route is not evidence that a licence has been granted or its conditions satisfied.

official_sources.name: Tree felling licence service
official_sources.fact: GOV.UK identifies tree felling as a legally controlled activity and links to the Forestry Commission licence application route.
official_sources.gate: Service availability is not parcel-specific confirmation that a licence is required, exempted, issued or sufficient for all other controls.

official_sources.name: Environmental Impact Assessments for woodland
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission guidance explains forestry EIA screening/consent for afforestation, deforestation, forest roads and quarries in England.
official_sources.gate: EIA screening, stage 1 decision or threshold context is not planning permission, felling permission or stage 2 consent.

official_sources.name: Definition of trees and woodland
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission guidance updated 11 July 2025 defines its regulatory interpretation of trees and woodland for the Forestry Act and forestry EIA regime.
official_sources.gate: This regulatory interpretation is explicitly scope-limited and must not be reused as a universal planning, habitat or ownership definition.

official_sources.name: The UK Forestry Standard
official_sources.fact: UKFS fifth edition is the government technical standard for sustainable forest management and applies in England from 1 October 2024.
official_sources.gate: UKFS compliance is not planning permission, grant award, felling licence or proof of exact parcel suitability.

official_sources.name: Trees and woodland guidance for local authorities
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission local-authority guidance published February 2026 and updated 17 July 2026 links planning, planting, protection and funding resources.
official_sources.gate: A local-authority guidance resource is not an adopted local policy, live TPO record, woodland consent or parcel decision.

official_sources.name: Tree planting and woodland creation: overview
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission overview covers funding, EIA, sustainable woodland creation and habitats/species protection in England.
official_sources.gate: Woodland creation policy or support does not prove a site can be planted, funded or consented without site-specific regulatory checks.

official_sources.name: Tree planting and woodland creation resources
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission resource hub published 21 May 2025 links planning, site preparation, planting, protection and long-term management guidance.
official_sources.gate: Resource links and good practice are not approvals, site surveys or exact development constraints.

official_sources.name: Woodland creation timeline: from planning to planting
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission timeline sets the staged process from site scoping through surveys, EIA/consultation, grant decision and planting.
official_sources.gate: Indicative process durations or Fast Track targets are not guaranteed delivery dates, consent or parcel viability.

official_sources.name: Woodland Creation Planning Grant
official_sources.fact: WCPG guidance updated 11 February 2026 funds preparation of a UKFS-compliant woodland creation design plan.
official_sources.gate: Planning-grant eligibility or award is not approval to plant and does not replace forestry EIA or other consents.

official_sources.name: Woodland Creation Planning Grant application form
official_sources.fact: WCPG application materials were updated in March/April 2026 and require mapped site and staged design information.
official_sources.gate: Application completeness or a mapped proposal is not grant award, EIA consent or exact parcel development permission.

official_sources.name: How the England Woodland Creation Offer works
official_sources.fact: EWCO guidance sets eligibility and states low-sensitivity Fast Track remains case-by-case and still requires complete UKFS-compliant evidence.
official_sources.gate: Low-sensitivity map coverage is not a green light, grant award, EIA consent or exact site suitability result.

official_sources.name: Guidance on how to apply for EWCO
official_sources.fact: Current EWCO application guidance requires necessary permissions/consents before works and describes the Woodland Creation Fast Track route.
official_sources.gate: An EWCO application, Fast Track request or eligibility response is not consent to plant or proof that all permissions are in place.

official_sources.name: Get England Woodland Creation Offer funding to plant woodland
official_sources.fact: The Forestry Commission EWCO collection consolidates current application, agreement, claims and woodland creation guidance.
official_sources.gate: Collection membership or scheme availability is not evidence of a site-specific agreement, payment or permission.

official_sources.name: Guidance on claiming your EWCO payments
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 22 June 2026 explains claims for completed capital works and maintenance payments under EWCO agreements.
official_sources.gate: A claim route or payment rule does not prove works are complete, compliant, inspected or paid on a target parcel.

official_sources.name: EWCO common land and shared grazing guidance
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 9 January 2026 sets additional EWCO requirements for registered common land and shared grazing.
official_sources.gate: EWCO common-land eligibility is not commons consent, proof of rights, exact legal boundary or planning permission.

official_sources.name: EWCO natural colonisation site assessment guidance
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 9 January 2026 requires a site assessment where natural colonisation is proposed under EWCO.
official_sources.gate: Natural-colonisation eligibility or nearby seed sources do not prove establishment success, consent or final woodland geometry.

official_sources.name: EWCO land manager authorisation
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission form published 8 June 2026 addresses management-control transfer where the applicant does not own the land.
official_sources.gate: Land-manager authorisation is not title ownership, planning permission, regulatory consent or proof of long-term site control.

official_sources.name: Tree planting and woodland creation: funding and advice
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission collection links current planning and woodland-creation grant/support routes including WCPG.
official_sources.gate: Funding availability is not a parcel-specific award, consent or viable development scenario.

official_sources.name: Where to find grants for trees and woodland
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission collection lists grants for woodland creation, management and tree health in England.
official_sources.gate: A listed grant scheme does not prove eligibility, award, delivery or regulatory approval for a site.

official_sources.name: Tree and woodland grants and incentives overview
official_sources.fact: The overview compares woodland creation, management, carbon and tree-health incentives and key eligibility parameters.
official_sources.gate: Grant sizes, minimum areas and incentive parameters are financing context, not planning or forestry consent.

official_sources.name: Public registers and consultation on forestry projects
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission guidance explains 21-day consultation registers and decision registers for relevant woodland creation, EIA and felling proposals.
official_sources.gate: A consultation-register entry, objection or publication is not the final Forestry Commission decision or parcel consent.

official_sources.name: Forestry Commissioners statement on consultation procedures
official_sources.fact: The Forestry Commissioners statement sets the revised consultation approach for woodland creation, felling and management applications.
official_sources.gate: Consultation completion or lack of repeated consultation does not imply approval; the regulatory/grant decision remains separate.

official_sources.name: How to appeal a decision by the Forestry Commission
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 7 July 2026 covers appeals against grant, felling licence, restocking/enforcement and forestry EIA decisions.
official_sources.gate: An appeal right, filing or hearing does not establish reversal, consent or parcel development status.

official_sources.name: Appeal against a restocking or enforcement notice
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission guidance updated 7 July 2026 explains appeals against restocking and enforcement notices.
official_sources.gate: Appeal status does not erase the underlying notice or prove compliance; exact notice, appeal and decision status are required.

official_sources.name: Report suspected illegal tree felling
official_sources.fact: Forestry Commission guidance explains checks, reporting and possible restocking/enforcement consequences for suspected unlicensed felling.
official_sources.gate: A report or suspicion is not proof of an offence, live enforcement notice or current parcel constraint.

official_sources.name: Tree preservation order data specification
official_sources.fact: Planning Data specification updated 10 April 2026 requires linked TPO, TPO-zone and individual-tree datasets with stable references and geometry fields.
official_sources.gate: Schema conformance is not proof that an authority dataset is complete, authoritative or current for an exact parcel.

official_sources.name: Planning Data tree preservation order dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 107,674 TPO records from 74 providers with collector and new-data dates of 24 July 2026, while noting some MHCLG-created data remains.
official_sources.gate: Platform TPO records require exact order/document and geometry linkage; mixed provenance must not be promoted to complete legal truth.

official_sources.name: Planning Data tree preservation zone dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 94,023 tree-preservation zones from 79 providers, collector run 22 July 2026, with some MHCLG-created data.
official_sources.gate: A zone overlap is screening evidence and must be reconciled with the exact live TPO order, zone type, dates and authoritative source.

official_sources.name: Planning Data tree dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data reports 247,862 tree records from 74 providers, collector run 22 July 2026, with mixed/MHCLG-created provenance noted.
official_sources.gate: Individual-tree platform data may be partial and must not be treated as a complete inventory of all protected trees or exact site constraints.

official_sources.name: Planning Data tree preservation zone type dataset
official_sources.fact: Planning Data defines three TPO-zone type codes: area, group and woodland.
official_sources.gate: A zone-type taxonomy is not evidence that a specific zone exists, is live, or applies to a target parcel.
